note: Frozen twin case table for pointer-scoped external reference composition. openbindings.openapi@1 section 6 ('Reference scope'): a reference that leaves the current document composes the value at the referenced JSON Pointer together with that value's transitive closure of references, and nothing else. Each case is a multi-document artifact plus the one verdict every engine must reach. The identical file is executed by openbindings-go's formats/openapi, by openapi-client/go, and by openbindings-ts's packages/openapi; a divergence in one fails the others' suites too. Authored from the OAS and JSON Reference text. No byte comes from a corpus specimen.

cases.name: defect-outside-the-composed-closure
cases.why: A dangling reference in a component the pointer never reaches is outside the composed closure, so the referencing artifact resolves (openbindings.openapi@1 section 6).

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: defect-inside-the-composed-closure
cases.why: A reference reachable from the referenced pointer, and unresolvable there, does make the referencing artifact unresolvable.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: defect-outside-the-closure-inside-the-same-component
cases.why: The composed value is the value AT the pointer, not the component that contains it: a sibling property of the same Schema Object is outside the closure.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Big/properties/kept"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: target-is-not-an-openapi-document
cases.why: No accepted edition requires a reference target to be a conforming OpenAPI Document; the OAS's own Reference Object examples address a bare schema file.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./fragments.yaml#/Thing"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: pointer-into-a-bare-json-schema-file
cases.why: A JSON Schema resource is a legal reference target; its own $defs are addressable and nothing outside the addressed pointer is composed.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./schema.json#/$defs/Widget"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: cycle-spanning-two-documents
cases.why: A cycle whose members are declared in different documents is composed like any other; both engines must cut it at the same members and name them from the declaring document.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./a.yaml#/components/schemas/Node"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

https://composition.example/a.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: A, version: "1"}
components:
  schemas:
    Node:
      type: object
      properties:
        peer: {$ref: "./b.yaml#/components/schemas/Peer"}

cases.name: relative-base-two-directories-up
cases.why: A relative reference resolves against the referring document's own address, so the closure pass and the resolver must join it the same way.

https://composition.example/spec/v1/open.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "../../shared/library.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: absolute-base-on-another-host
cases.why: An absolute reference identifies its resource without the referring document's base; the same scope rule applies.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "https://library.example/shared.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: target-file-is-not-well-formed
cases.why: Parsing is not scoping: a target that cannot be read as a document fails the reference that reaches it, whatever the pointer would have selected.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./broken.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

https://composition.example/broken.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Broken, version: "1"}
components:
  schemas:
    Used:
      type: array
      items:
      type: integer

cases.name: unreachable-resource-referenced-only-outside-the-closure
cases.why: A resource reached only from outside the composed closure is never retrieved, so its availability cannot decide the artifact.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: defect-outside-a-second-hop-closure
cases.why: The closure is transitive: a second document reached through the first composes only what the first reference's value reaches.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./a.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

https://composition.example/a.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: A, version: "1"}
components:
  schemas:
    Used:
      type: object
      properties:
        deep: {$ref: "./b.yaml#/components/schemas/Deep"}

cases.name: defect-inside-a-second-hop-closure
cases.why: Transitivity cuts both ways: a defect the second hop's value does reach refuses the artifact.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:

info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}

  /items:

        required: true

          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./a.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

https://composition.example/a.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: A, version: "1"}
components:
  schemas:
    Used:
      type: object
      properties:
        deep: {$ref: "./b.yaml#/components/schemas/Deep"}

cases.name: pointer-below-a-reference
cases.why: A pointer whose path runs through a reference reaches the position the resolved value has there; the reference it passes through is itself composed.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Alias/properties/name"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: whole-file-reference-composes-the-file
cases.why: A reference with no fragment addresses the resource root, so the composed value is the whole file and a defect anywhere in it is inside the closure.
